statements.quote: To operationalize our treatment and investigate the effects of using GLMs for brainstorming, we developed a brainstorming app without social cues (Fig. 5), allowing adding, editing, and removing ideas based on prior research (Di Fede et al. 2022; Memmert and Tavanapour 2023), following the approach of adapting – through task-specific prompting – and integrating an existing GLM (see Schneider et al. 2024).
statements.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sect. 3.3, app materials

statements.quote: Online Appendix A (available online via http://link.springer.com) depicts the user’s interaction with the app and the information flow to and from the GLM.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sect. 3.3, Online Appendix A

statements.quote: At every ‘‘Generate ideas’’ click, the backend filled a pre-defined prompt template (cf. Memmert et al. 2024a; see Fig. 6; full explanation in Online Appendix B) with the brainstorming question and the number of ideas per request, and the live canvas state:
statements.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sect. 3.3, Online Appendix B; sentence introducing the input lists

statements.quote: The post-survey contained open- and closed-ended questions (Tab. 1, Online Appendix C for full questionnaire).
statements.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 1033), Sect. 3.5, Online Appendix C

statements.quote: The operationalization for all brainstorming performance metrics and variables is detailed in Online Appendix D.
statements.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 1033), Sect. 3.5, Online Appendix D

statements.quote: We use two sources of data: the participants’ interaction data from the brainstorming sessions, such as the number of ideas or the number of suggestion requests, and the survey data, allowing us to contrast actual behavior with the participants’ perception. For the evaluation of the shortlisted ideas, the ideas were randomized, exported, and evaluated.
statements.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 1033), Sect. 3.6, data sources and preparation

statements.quote: For statistical analysis, we used the JASP statistics software (JASP 2023).
statements.locator: PDF pp. 11-12 (journal pp. 1033-1034), Sect. 3.6; sentence crosses the page break

statements.quote: The finalized coding scheme (Online Appendix E) was used to analyze the remaining material. Individual answers to the open-ended survey questions were used as the unit of analysis, and illustrative quotes are reported in the results section.
statements.locator: PDF p. 12 (journal p. 1034), Sect. 3.6, Online Appendix E

statements.quote: We therefore provide qualitative interview data to contextualize both significant and nonsignificant quantitative findings.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12599-025-00974-y.

notes:
Checked on 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without login or personal identifiers. Read all 843 lines (124,086 characters) of the saved markdown, covering the entire 25-page PDF through its references. Checked the relevant PDF pages with PyMuPDF. Online Appendices A-E are outside the saved PDF and could not be read because the requested supplemental endpoint returned a bot challenge; no local supplement was found among the matching library filenames.

No statement in the saved paper offers participant data or analysis code publicly or on request, and no preregistration or research-data repository is named. The form's data_url and code_url are empty. The qualitative-data wording in Sect. 5.4 accompanies illustrative quotations in Sect. 4.4; it does not promise a downloadable dataset. Acknowledgements name BMBF project HyMeKI funding but no data source or deposit.

Quotes were extracted from the PDF, with line wrapping, discretionary line-end hyphens and typographic ligatures normalized. The PDF supplies 'information flow' in the Appendix A sentence, where the markdown drops 'flow'; PDF links also confirm the hyphenated article DOI that the markdown scrambles. Article text is licensed CC BY 4.0 (PDF p. 22); this is not treated as verification of a separate dataset license.

All completed repository search requests returned HTTP 200. The two initial Zenodo requests with size=100 returned HTTP 400: anonymous page size cannot exceed 25. They were repeated with size=25; the failed requests have null result counts. Counts are repository-reported totals, not counts of relevant datasets. DataCite query Memmert was paged through all 392 metadata records (100, 100, 100, 92); candidates were screened for Lucas, brainstorming, or the article DOI, and all 24 focused creator-query records were reviewed. Zenodo query Memmert was paged through all 69 records (25, 25, 19).

Search endpoints: https://api.datacite.org/dois?query=<query>&page[size]=100; https://zenodo.org/api/records?q=<query>&size=25; https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/search?q=<query>&per_page=100; https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/?filter[title]=<query>&page[size]=100. Queries were URL-encoded; DataCite pagination used page[number] and Zenodo used page. OSF searches with an author's name match node titles, not contributor fields, so those searches alone cannot exclude projects under other titles.

The relevant URLs in searches refer to the matching ZORA article record, not confirmed research data. The other DataCite title-stem hit is the distinct conference paper 'The Role of Creative Ability and Tool-Support for Brainstorming Performance' (10.5167/uzh-436328). Other author hits are publications or unrelated course materials; none was identified as this paper's data deposit. Harvard's three Memmert hits concern Daniel Memmert's sport stimuli or equipment bearing the Memmert name. Zenodo's Memmert AND Lucas hit is the unrelated taxonomic record Quedius hispanicus (7503703).

The three OSF Memmert-title hits concern Daniel Memmert's attention studies (oabzc, 2hk4c, wxgiz). Among the 18 Brainstorming hits, node/contributor API checks (HTTP 200) excluded plausible ambiguous records: zf3s2 is 'ChatGPT Decreases Idea Diversity in Brainstorming' by Lennart Meincke, Gideon Nave and Christian Terwiesch; kt6j2 is by Nicolas Michinov; mcqxs and 7ajz5 are unrelated projects created in 2017 and 2018 with different contributors. These are not counted as deposits for c098.

Other statement-link check: http://link.springer.com redirected to https://link.springer.com/ and returned HTTP 200 with 'Client Challenge'; http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ redirected to HTTPS and returned HTTP 200 with the CC BY 4.0 deed. Publisher and ZORA bot responses were not bypassed. Empty file lists and null counts indicate an unverified inventory, not a confirmed absence of files.

No public participant-level or participant-linked output file was read. Therefore the final.open_items about randomized/analyzed/outcome-specific arm counts and participant-level SDs/SEs remain unresolved. Per-person means by arm and text/idea diversity cannot be computed from verified public data. The Fig. 8c interval type, Appendix D Good-Idea-Count threshold, possible shared sample, and human-fluency p-value discrepancy also remain unresolved. Status none_found means no confirmed public participant-data deposit was found; it is not proof that no deposit exists, especially because the supplemental files were inaccessible. No evidence establishes an account requirement or on-request availability.
